sides.name: Germany (9th Army, 4th Panzer Army, Army Detachment Kempf)
sides.note: Strength (Wikipedia infobox citing Frieser and Zetterling/Frankson): 780,900 men, 2,928 tanks and assault guns (low ~2,450 = tanks only), 9,966 guns and mortars (low excludes light mortars, educated), 2,110 aircraft. infantry_line ~45-50% of strength across ~50 divisions (17 panzer/panzergrenadier), educated split. Fighter/strike split of Luftflotte 4 and 6 is educated. Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 1943 = anchor 8): weapons/armor 8.1-8.2 (Tiger, Panther, Ferdinand debut); logistics 7.6 (horse-drawn infantry divisions, rail-fed). Ratings: command 0.75 (trained staff, Manstein/Model, but a delayed and predictable offensive); morale 0.65; training 0.7. No surprise: the Soviets knew the plan and timing.

sides.name: Soviet Union (Central and Voronezh Fronts; Steppe Front as reinforcement)
sides.note: Strength (Wikipedia citing Glantz/House, Zetterling/Frankson, Healy): Central Front 711,575 men (510,983 combat), Voronezh Front 625,591 (446,236 combat); together ~1,300,000 men, 3,600 tanks (1,061 light T-60/T-70), ~20,000 guns and mortars, 2,792 aircraft (Bergstrom). infantry_line ~55-65% of the 957,219 'combat soldiers' plus rifle troops counted elsewhere, educated. Reinforcement day 6 (11-12 July): Steppe Front had 573,195 men (449,133 combat) and ~1,600 tanks in reserve; 5th Guards Tank Army (~650-850 tanks) and 5th Guards Army were committed at Prokhorovka; mid assumes about half the front engaged, high = all of it (Steppe Front's 70,085 casualties in the defensive operation show heavy commitment). Tech: fortification 8.3 (eight defensive belts, e.g. 6th Guards Army: 69,688 AT + 64,430 AP mines in its first belt alone); ISR 7.9 (strategic warning of timing and axes). Ratings: command 0.75 (Zhukov, Vasilevsky, Rokossovsky, Vatutin; proven staff system by 1943); morale 0.8 after Stalingrad; training 0.55.

outcome.note: Citadel 5-16 July 1943 (northern face stalled by 14 July; Soviet defensive operation officially 5-23 July). German: 54,182 casualties during Citadel (Frieser, from German archive records); high allows later counts to 23 July. Soviet: 177,847 for the Kursk defensive operation (Krivosheev: Central 33,897, Voronezh 73,892, Steppe 70,085); high allows for later authors who judge Krivosheev low (unfetched, educated margin). Material: German 252-323 AFVs destroyed; Soviet 1,614-1,956 tanks/SPGs destroyed.
